rules.title: Setup answer file is readable by non-admins
rules.subject: {path}
rules.why: Unattend and sysprep answer files often hold the local administrator password, base64-encoded at most.
rules.fix: Delete the file if setup is finished. Otherwise check it for <Password> and <AdministratorPassword> elements, change any password it holds, and restrict the file to Administrators and SYSTEM.

rules.title: Setup answer file left on disk
rules.subject: {path}
rules.why: Non-admins can't read it, but answer files often hold the local administrator password, and anyone who gets admin rights or a disk image can.
rules.fix: Delete it if setup is finished, and change any password it holds.

rules.title: Autologon password stored in the registry
rules.subject: {default_username}
rules.why: Winlogon's DefaultPassword is stored in plaintext under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon, a key every user can read.
rules.fix: Delete the DefaultPassword value and change that account's password. If autologon is really needed, set it up with Sysinternals Autologon, which stores the password as an LSA secret instead.

rules.title: PowerShell history file present
rules.subject: {path}
rules.why: PSReadLine saves every command typed in PowerShell, including passwords and tokens passed on the command line.
rules.fix: Review it and clear anything sensitive (the path is (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath). Keep secrets off the command line, or use Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing for sensitive sessions.
